task: Find the current CEO of a recently-acquired startup
user_request: Who runs Lumio Robotics right now?
agent_action: Agent called web_search with query 'Lumio Robotics CEO' but omitted any recency/date constraint (no 'after:2025' filter and no time_range param), then quoted the top result naming a CEO who left in 2023.
failure_type: Omitted recency filter on search query
root_cause: The web_search call lacked a date-scoping argument (the API supports a `recency`/`time_range` parameter), so stale 2023 articles outranked the post-acquisition leadership change.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the top organic result reflects the present. Wrong because evergreen SEO pages from 2023 outrank fresh news, and 'right now' demands recency scoping. Avoidable by passing a recency/time_range filter or adding an explicit year and cross-checking the publish date before quoting.
impact: User cited an out-of-date executive in a partnership email and had to send a correction.
correct_action: Re-run web_search with a recency window (e.g. last 6 months) or an explicit date qualifier, open the most recent source, and confirm the publish date before naming a person.
recovery_plan: Notice the cited article predates the acquisition
Re-issue web_search with a recency/time_range filter
Open the freshest source and read the publish date
Confirm the current CEO from an authoritative recent page
Send the corrected name with the source date
evaluation_criteria: Checks the search call included a recency/date-scoping parameter
Verifies the agent read the publish date of the source before answering
Flags answers drawn from results with no time filter

task: Answer a policy question from the internal handbook via RAG
user_request: What's our parental leave policy for the EU offices?
agent_action: Agent ran vector_store.query with the text 'parental leave policy' but omitted the metadata `filter={'region':'EU'}`, retrieving the US-region chunk and answering with 12 weeks instead of the EU statutory entitlement.
root_cause: The retrieval call left out the `filter` argument keyed on the `region` metadata field, so the nearest-neighbor chunk by embedding similarity came from the US handbook section.
why_it_failed: Assumption: semantic similarity alone would surface the EU policy. Wrong because US and EU policy chunks are near-identical in wording and embed close together; only the region metadata disambiguates them. Avoidable by passing the region filter the index was designed with.
impact: User relayed the wrong leave entitlement to an EU employee, creating an HR compliance discrepancy.
correct_action: Re-query the vector store with `filter={'region':'EU'}` and cite the EU handbook chunk ID in the answer.
recovery_plan: Detect the cited chunk's region metadata is 'US'
Re-run vector_store.query with the EU region filter
Verify the returned chunk's source document is the EU handbook
Re-answer with the EU entitlement and chunk citation
Add a region-filter requirement to the RAG prompt
evaluation_criteria: Checks the retrieval call set a metadata filter matching the asked region
Verifies the cited chunk's region matches the question
Flags answers grounded in an unfiltered nearest-neighbor result

task: Share a finance folder with a new contractor via Google Drive MCP
user_request: Give the new contractor access to the 2026 Budget folder.
agent_action: Agent called gdrive.permissions.create on folder 1A2b_BudgetFY26 with role 'reader' and type 'user' but omitted the `emailAddress` field, so the API created an unspecified/empty grantee that silently resolved to a domain-wide entry in this workspace config.
failure_type: Omitted grantee identifier on permission grant
root_cause: gdrive.permissions.create requires `emailAddress` when type='user'; it was absent, and the workspace's default handling broadened the grant beyond the intended single contractor.
why_it_failed: Assumption: passing type='user' was enough to scope the grant. Wrong because without `emailAddress` the API has no specific principal and the grant defaulted wide. Avoidable by always supplying the explicit contractor email and reading back the created permission.
impact: A financial-budget folder became accessible far beyond one contractor until the permission was audited and revoked.
correct_action: Call gdrive.permissions.create with role='reader', type='user', and emailAddress set to the contractor's exact address, then list permissions to confirm only that principal was added.
recovery_plan: List permissions on the budget folder via gdrive.permissions.list
Identify and delete the over-broad permission entry
Re-create the grant with the contractor's explicit emailAddress
Verify only the intended principal has access
Notify the owner of the brief exposure window
evaluation_criteria: Checks the permission call included an explicit emailAddress grantee
Verifies a post-grant read confirmed the principal scope
Flags any user-type grant missing a concrete principal

task: Send a release-notes email to the beta list via Gmail MCP
user_request: Email the beta testers the v2.7 release notes.
agent_action: Agent called gmail.messages.send with the 12 beta-tester addresses in the `to` field instead of `bcc`, omitting the `bcc` parameter entirely, exposing every tester's email to all recipients.
failure_type: Omitted bcc, recipients placed in to
root_cause: For a bulk announcement the addresses belonged in the `bcc` argument; that field was never set and all addresses went into `to`, leaking the full recipient list.
why_it_failed: Assumption: any recipient field delivers the mail, so `to` is fine. Wrong because a multi-recipient external blast requires `bcc` to protect addresses. Avoidable by recognizing a list send and populating `bcc` with `to` set to a no-reply sender.
impact: All 12 beta testers' personal email addresses were disclosed to each other, a privacy incident requiring an apology.
correct_action: Send with the testers in `bcc`, `to` set to a no-reply or the sender address, and confirm the recipient layout before sending.
recovery_plan: Recognize recipient addresses were exposed in `to`
Send a follow-up apology acknowledging the disclosure
Re-send the notes using `bcc` for the recipient list
Add a bulk-send guard that routes lists to bcc
Document the incident for privacy review
evaluation_criteria: Checks bulk recipients were placed in bcc, not to/cc
Verifies the agent distinguished a list blast from a direct email
Flags a multi-external-recipient send with an empty bcc

task: Run a dependency CVE scan and report criticals
user_request: Scan our service for known-vulnerable dependencies and list the criticals.
agent_action: Agent ran `npm audit` at the repo root but omitted `--omit=dev` is-not-the-issue; it omitted the `--production`/workspace scope and ran without `--audit-level`, then also failed to pass the lockfile path so it scanned only the root manifest and missed the three workspace packages where the criticals lived.
root_cause: In an npm workspaces monorepo, `npm audit` needs `--workspaces` (or per-workspace invocation) to traverse child packages; that flag was absent so child lockfile entries were never evaluated.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a root-level audit covers the whole monorepo. Wrong because workspaces isolate dependency trees and the root scan skips children unless `--workspaces` is set. Avoidable by detecting the workspaces field in package.json and passing the workspace scope.
impact: Three critical CVEs in workspace packages were reported as 'none found', leaving them unpatched in the release.
correct_action: Detect the monorepo layout and run `npm audit --workspaces` (or iterate each workspace), aggregating criticals across all child packages.
recovery_plan: Notice package.json declares a workspaces array
Re-run npm audit with --workspaces enabled
Aggregate critical findings across all child packages
Cross-check against a second scanner (osv-scanner)
Re-issue the criticals report with full coverage
evaluation_criteria: Checks the audit invocation scoped all workspace packages
Verifies findings were aggregated across child lockfiles
Flags a monorepo audit run only at the root

task: Refund a customer charge via Stripe
user_request: Refund the duplicate charge for customer cus_Kd9, the $80 one.
agent_action: Agent called stripe.refunds.create with the customer id only, omitting the `charge` (or `payment_intent`) parameter, so Stripe refunded against the customer's most recent charge — a different, legitimate $80 charge — instead of the duplicate.
failure_type: Omitted target charge identifier on refund
root_cause: stripe.refunds.create needs an explicit `charge` or `payment_intent` to target; without it the integration defaulted to the latest charge, which was not the duplicate.
why_it_failed: Assumption: naming the customer uniquely identifies the charge to refund. Wrong because the customer had multiple $80 charges and the API needs the specific charge id. Avoidable by listing the customer's charges, identifying the duplicate's id, and passing it explicitly.
impact: A valid charge was refunded by mistake while the actual duplicate remained, requiring a re-charge and customer apology.
correct_action: List the customer's charges, find the duplicate by amount and timestamp, and call stripe.refunds.create with that exact charge id.
recovery_plan: List charges for cus_Kd9 via stripe.charges.list
Identify which charge was wrongly refunded
Re-create the legitimate charge or note it for reconciliation
Refund the true duplicate by its explicit charge id
Confirm both charges' final states with the customer
evaluation_criteria: Checks the refund call specified an explicit charge/payment_intent
Verifies the targeted charge matched the duplicate by amount and time
Flags a refund that relied on a default 'latest charge'

task: Compile a list of grant deadlines from a funder's site
user_request: List all the open grant deadlines on the SciFund portal.
agent_action: Agent paginated the listing via browser but called the portal's results endpoint without the `status=open` query parameter, returning the default mixed view, then listed several already-closed grants as open.
failure_type: Omitted status filter on listing query
root_cause: The portal's results API filters by a `status` parameter; with it absent the endpoint returned all grants regardless of state, including closed ones.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the default listing shows only open grants. Wrong because the default view mixes open and closed and only `status=open` narrows it. Avoidable by inspecting the portal's filter controls and passing status=open, or checking each row's deadline against today.
impact: User wasted effort preparing for two grants whose deadlines had already passed.
correct_action: Re-request the listing with `status=open`, or filter rows whose deadline is on/after today, before compiling the list.
recovery_plan: Compare each listed deadline against the current date
Re-query the portal with status=open
Drop grants whose deadline has passed
Re-compile the open-only list
Note the date checked for transparency
evaluation_criteria: Checks the listing request applied an open-status filter
Verifies each listed deadline is on/after the current date
Flags inclusion of closed items in an 'open' list

task: Build a RAG index over the contracts folder
user_request: Index all our vendor contracts so we can search them.
agent_action: Agent called embeddings.create and upsert for each document but omitted the `namespace` (tenant) argument on pinecone.upsert, writing all vectors into the default namespace shared with another client's data, so later queries mixed tenants.
root_cause: The Pinecone index is multi-tenant by namespace; upsert without a `namespace` argument wrote to the default namespace instead of the contracts tenant, co-mingling vectors.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a single index is automatically per-project. Wrong because this index partitions tenants by namespace and upsert defaults to ''. Avoidable by passing the contracts namespace on every upsert and query, matching the index's tenancy design.
impact: Contract search returned chunks belonging to a different client, a data-isolation breach requiring re-index and cleanup.
correct_action: Re-upsert all contract vectors with the explicit contracts namespace and ensure every subsequent query passes the same namespace.
recovery_plan: Detect cross-tenant chunks appearing in query results
Delete the mis-placed vectors from the default namespace
Re-upsert all contracts into the dedicated namespace
Verify queries with the namespace return only contract chunks
Add a namespace-required check to the ingest pipeline
evaluation_criteria: Checks every upsert and query supplied the tenant namespace
Verifies no cross-tenant chunks appear in results
Flags writes to the default/empty namespace in a multi-tenant index

task: Export the latest design doc from Google Drive MCP
user_request: Download the Design Spec doc as a PDF.
agent_action: Agent called gdrive.files.export on the Google Doc fileId but omitted the required `mimeType` parameter, so the export call errored and the agent reported it 'couldn't find a PDF version' rather than supplying the target format.
root_cause: gdrive.files.export requires a target `mimeType` (e.g. application/pdf) for native Google Docs; the call omitted it and returned a 400, which the agent misread as a missing file.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the export endpoint infers PDF by default. Wrong because Google Docs export mandates an explicit target mimeType. Avoidable by passing mimeType='application/pdf' as the export format the user requested.
impact: User received no file and a misleading 'no PDF exists' message, blocking the handoff until retried.
correct_action: Call gdrive.files.export with mimeType='application/pdf' for the Doc's fileId and return the exported bytes.
recovery_plan: Recognize the 400 was a missing-format error, not a missing file
Re-call gdrive.files.export with mimeType='application/pdf'
Confirm the response content-type is PDF
Deliver the exported file to the user
Correct the earlier 'no PDF' message
evaluation_criteria: Checks the export call specified a target mimeType
Verifies the returned content matches the requested PDF format
Flags treating a missing-parameter 400 as a missing file

task: Search a mailbox for an invoice via Gmail MCP
user_request: Find the Acme invoice from last March and forward it to finance.
agent_action: Agent called gmail.messages.list with q='Acme invoice' but omitted the date operators (`after:`/`before:`) and the `maxResults` was left at default 100, returning the most recent Acme thread and forwarding this year's invoice instead of last March's.
failure_type: Omitted date-range operators in mail query
root_cause: The Gmail search `q` lacked `after:2025/03/01 before:2025/04/01`, so results were ordered by recency and the wrong-year invoice was selected.
why_it_failed: Assumption: 'last March' would be matched implicitly by relevance. Wrong because Gmail search has no temporal sense without date operators and defaults to recency. Avoidable by adding after:/before: bounding the target month before picking a message.
impact: Finance received the wrong invoice and had to request the correct one, delaying reconciliation.
correct_action: Query with `from:acme invoice after:2025/03/01 before:2025/04/01`, confirm the message date, then forward the correct invoice.
recovery_plan: Check the forwarded message's date against 'last March'
Re-run gmail.messages.list with after:/before: date operators
Open the matching March message and verify the invoice
Forward the correct message to finance
Send finance a note superseding the wrong forward
evaluation_criteria: Checks the mail query included date-range operators matching the ask
Verifies the selected message's date falls in the requested month
Flags selection of the most-recent thread without date scoping

task: Run SAST and report high-severity findings on the PR diff
user_request: Run Semgrep on this branch and flag the high-severity issues.
agent_action: Agent invoked `semgrep scan` without the `--config` argument, so it ran with no rules loaded, reported 'No findings', and the agent concluded the branch was clean.
failure_type: Omitted ruleset config on SAST scan
root_cause: `semgrep scan` requires a `--config` (ruleset/registry id or path); with it absent Semgrep loads no rules and trivially returns zero findings.
why_it_failed: Assumption: Semgrep applies a sensible default ruleset automatically. Wrong because without --config it scans against an empty rule set. Avoidable by passing --config=auto or the org's ruleset path and sanity-checking that rules were actually loaded.
impact: A branch with an injection flaw was reported clean and merged, shipping the vulnerability.
correct_action: Run `semgrep scan --config p/owasp-top-ten` (or the org ruleset) and confirm the rule count loaded before trusting a zero-findings result.
recovery_plan: Notice Semgrep reported 0 rules loaded
Re-run semgrep with an explicit --config ruleset
Review high-severity findings on the branch
Block or fix the merge if issues are found
Add a CI check asserting a non-empty ruleset
evaluation_criteria: Checks the SAST invocation supplied a non-empty ruleset config
Verifies the agent confirmed rules were loaded before reporting clean
Flags a 'no findings' result from a scan with no config

task: Create a subscription for a new customer via Stripe
user_request: Subscribe cus_7TpL to the Pro monthly plan.
agent_action: Agent called stripe.subscriptions.create with customer and the price id but omitted no-wait — it omitted the `idempotency_key` header; a transient timeout triggered the agent's retry and two identical subscriptions were created, double-billing the customer.
root_cause: stripe.subscriptions.create was sent without an `idempotency_key`; when the first call timed out and the agent retried, Stripe treated it as a distinct request and created a second subscription.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a retry after a timeout is safe. Wrong because without an idempotency key Stripe cannot dedupe the retried create, so the customer got two subscriptions. Avoidable by setting a stable idempotency_key so the retry collapses onto the first request.
impact: Customer was billed twice for the Pro plan, requiring cancellation of the duplicate and a refund.
correct_action: Send stripe.subscriptions.create with a deterministic idempotency_key; on timeout, retry with the same key so Stripe returns the original result instead of creating a duplicate.
recovery_plan: List subscriptions for cus_7TpL and detect the duplicate
Cancel the duplicate subscription via stripe.subscriptions.cancel
Refund or credit the extra charge
Re-issue the create with a stable idempotency_key
Add idempotency keys to all create retries in the workflow
evaluation_criteria: Checks create calls carried an idempotency_key
Verifies retries reused the same key rather than generating a new request
Flags a duplicate resource produced by a key-less retry

task: Get the precise altitude of a mountain for a report
user_request: What's the elevation of Mount Toubkal in meters?
agent_action: Agent used the site's unit-toggle API via browser but called the conversion endpoint without the `units=metric` parameter, read the default-imperial figure, and reported 13,671 (feet) as if it were meters.
root_cause: The data endpoint returns imperial by default unless `units=metric` is passed; the parameter was omitted so the feet value was taken as meters.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the displayed number was already in the requested unit. Wrong because the endpoint defaults to feet and needs an explicit units arg. Avoidable by passing units=metric or noticing the value is implausibly large for meters and reconciling.
impact: The report stated an elevation roughly 3.3x too high until a reviewer caught the unit error.
correct_action: Request the figure with units=metric (or convert feet→meters explicitly) and label the unit in the answer.
recovery_plan: Notice 13,671 m is implausible for this peak
Re-fetch with units=metric or convert from feet
Confirm against a second source's metric figure
Report the corrected ~4,167 m value with the unit
Always pass and label units going forward
evaluation_criteria: Checks the request specified the metric unit parameter
Verifies the reported value is plausible for the unit stated
Flags a value taken in the endpoint's default unit

task: Answer from the most relevant section of a long PDF via RAG
user_request: What does our SLA say about credit eligibility for downtime?
agent_action: Agent called retriever.search with k left unset so it defaulted to top_k=1 and returned a single chunk, omitting the `top_k`/multi-chunk parameter; the one chunk covered downtime definitions but not the credit-eligibility clause, so the agent answered 'the SLA does not specify'.
root_cause: retriever.search defaulted to returning one chunk because `top_k` was not supplied; the credit-eligibility text lived in an adjacent chunk that was never retrieved.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the single best chunk contains the full answer. Wrong because the relevant clause spanned a neighboring chunk that top_k=1 excluded. Avoidable by setting top_k to retrieve several chunks and reading across them before concluding absence.
impact: User was told the SLA was silent on credits when it in fact specifies them, risking a wrong response to a customer.
correct_action: Re-run retriever.search with top_k=6, read all returned chunks, and synthesize the credit-eligibility clause if present.
recovery_plan: Suspect a single-chunk answer missed adjacent context
Re-run retriever.search with a larger top_k
Read across the returned chunks for the credit clause
Re-answer with the eligibility terms and chunk citations
Set a sensible default top_k in the RAG config
evaluation_criteria: Checks top_k was set high enough to cover adjacent context
Verifies the agent read multiple chunks before claiming absence
Flags a 'not specified' answer derived from a single chunk

task: List recent files in a shared drive via Google Drive MCP
user_request: Show me the files added to the Marketing shared drive this week.
agent_action: Agent called gdrive.files.list with a name query but omitted the `driveId`, `corpora='drive'`, and `includeItemsFromAllDrives=true` parameters, so the call searched only My Drive and returned nothing from the shared drive.
root_cause: Querying a shared drive requires `corpora='drive'`, the `driveId`, and `includeItemsFromAllDrives=true`/`supportsAllDrives=true`; these were absent so the search defaulted to the user's My Drive corpus.
why_it_failed: Assumption: files.list searches all drives by default. Wrong because the API scopes to My Drive unless shared-drive parameters are supplied. Avoidable by resolving the Marketing driveId and passing the all-drives flags.
impact: User was told no files were added this week when several were, causing a missed review.
correct_action: Resolve the Marketing driveId, then call gdrive.files.list with corpora='drive', driveId set, includeItemsFromAllDrives=true, and a modifiedTime filter for this week.
recovery_plan: Notice the empty result contradicts known activity
Resolve the shared drive's driveId via gdrive.drives.list
Re-run files.list with all-drives scoping parameters
Apply a modifiedTime filter for the current week
Return the actual recent files
evaluation_criteria: Checks the list call included shared-drive scoping parameters
Verifies a driveId was resolved before querying
Flags an empty shared-drive result from a My-Drive-only query

task: Reply within an existing email thread via Gmail MCP
user_request: Reply to the customer on the open support thread that we've shipped the fix.
agent_action: Agent called gmail.messages.send with the recipient and body but omitted the `threadId` and the `In-Reply-To`/`References` headers, so the reply started a brand-new thread instead of threading under the support conversation.
root_cause: To thread a reply, the send needs `threadId` plus In-Reply-To/References headers; all were absent, so Gmail created a standalone message.
why_it_failed: Assumption: matching the subject line is enough to thread a reply. Wrong because Gmail threads by message-id references and threadId, not subject alone. Avoidable by fetching the original message's threadId and Message-ID and including them on the send.
impact: The customer received a disconnected email, breaking the support thread's continuity and confusing the conversation history.
correct_action: Fetch the original message, then send the reply with its threadId and In-Reply-To/References headers set so it threads correctly.
recovery_plan: Notice the reply created a new thread
Fetch the original support message's threadId and Message-ID
Re-send the reply with threadId and reference headers
Confirm the message appears within the original thread
Optionally delete the orphaned standalone reply
evaluation_criteria: Checks the reply send included threadId and reference headers
Verifies the message landed in the original thread
Flags a reply that relied on subject matching alone

task: Scan a container image for CVEs before release
user_request: Trivy-scan the payments image and fail if there are any critical CVEs.
agent_action: Agent ran `trivy image payments:2.7` without the `--severity CRITICAL` filter and without `--exit-code 1`, so it printed a long mixed list, exited 0, and the agent reported the gate 'passed' despite a critical present.
failure_type: Omitted severity filter and exit-code gate
root_cause: Without `--severity CRITICAL` and `--exit-code 1`, Trivy neither isolates criticals nor signals failure via exit status, so the release gate could not detect the critical CVE.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a successful scan command means no blocking vulnerabilities. Wrong because exit code 0 just means the scan ran, not that it was clean. Avoidable by passing --severity CRITICAL with --exit-code 1 so a critical fails the command.
impact: An image with a critical CVE was promoted to release because the gate reported a false pass.
correct_action: Run `trivy image --severity CRITICAL --exit-code 1 payments:2.7` and treat a non-zero exit as a hard gate failure.
recovery_plan: Re-run Trivy with --severity CRITICAL --exit-code 1
Observe the non-zero exit indicating a critical CVE
Block the release of payments:2.7
Patch or rebuild the base image to remediate
Wire the severity gate into the release pipeline
evaluation_criteria: Checks the scan applied a severity filter and exit-code gate
Verifies the agent used exit status, not command success, as the gate
Flags a 'passed' verdict from a scan with no failing condition set

task: Issue a partial refund on a Stripe payment
user_request: Refund $25 of the $100 charge ch_9aQ to the customer.
agent_action: Agent called stripe.refunds.create with `charge=ch_9aQ` but omitted the `amount` parameter, so Stripe defaulted to a full refund and returned the customer the entire $100 instead of $25.
root_cause: stripe.refunds.create refunds the full charge when `amount` is omitted; the partial-refund amount (2500 cents) was never supplied.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the refund would default to the requested partial amount from context. Wrong because Stripe defaults to a full refund when amount is absent. Avoidable by passing amount=2500 (cents) explicitly for the $25 partial.
impact: The customer was over-refunded by $75, a revenue loss requiring a re-charge or write-off.
correct_action: Call stripe.refunds.create with charge=ch_9aQ and amount=2500, confirming the cents value before submitting.
recovery_plan: Detect the refund amount equaled the full charge
Retrieve the refund to confirm $100 was returned
Re-charge or invoice the customer for the $75 overage with consent
Document the corrected $25 partial refund
Add an explicit-amount check for partial refunds
evaluation_criteria: Checks the refund call set an explicit amount in cents
Verifies the refunded amount matched the requested partial
Flags a full refund produced by an omitted amount

task: Pull the API rate limits from vendor docs
user_request: What's the rate limit for the v2 endpoint on the Helix API?
agent_action: Agent fetched the docs URL but omitted the documentation version selector (no `?version=v2` query param), landed on the v1 page that the docs default to, and reported the v1 limit of 60 req/min as the v2 limit.
failure_type: Omitted version param, wrong doc page
root_cause: The docs site renders the version chosen by a `version` query parameter; without it the page defaulted to v1, whose rate limit differs from v2's.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the docs landing page reflects v2. Wrong because the site defaults to v1 unless version=v2 is passed. Avoidable by selecting the v2 version in the URL or the version switcher and confirming the page header reads v2.
impact: User configured a client to the wrong rate limit, risking throttling under the actual v2 ceiling.
correct_action: Fetch the docs with version=v2 (or use the version switcher), confirm the page is v2, and report that endpoint's limit.
recovery_plan: Check the docs page header showed v1, not v2
Re-fetch the docs with version=v2 selected
Confirm the page header reads v2
Report the v2 endpoint's actual rate limit
Cite the versioned URL used
evaluation_criteria: Checks the docs request selected the asked API version
Verifies the page rendered matches that version
Flags an answer taken from a default-version docs page

task: Retrieve only this customer's docs in a multi-tenant RAG search
user_request: Summarize the support tickets we have on file for tenant globex.
agent_action: Agent ran weaviate.graphql search on the SupportTicket class with a nearText operator but omitted the `where` filter on `tenantId`, so the search returned tickets across all tenants and the summary mixed in another customer's tickets.
root_cause: The search lacked a `where` clause constraining `tenantId='globex'`, so nearText ranked semantically similar tickets regardless of tenant ownership.
why_it_failed: Assumption: nearText relevance would naturally return only globex tickets. Wrong because tickets across tenants are textually similar and only the tenant filter isolates them. Avoidable by adding the where filter on tenantId, which the schema indexes for exactly this.
impact: Another customer's ticket content leaked into globex's summary, a confidentiality breach.
correct_action: Re-run the search with a where filter on tenantId='globex' combined with nearText, and verify every returned object's tenantId before summarizing.
recovery_plan: Detect non-globex tenantIds in the returned objects
Re-run the query with a where filter on tenantId='globex'
Verify all results belong to the globex tenant
Re-generate the summary from tenant-scoped tickets only
Add a mandatory tenant filter to the search wrapper
evaluation_criteria: Checks the search applied a tenant where-filter
Verifies all returned objects share the requested tenantId
Flags a multi-tenant search relying on relevance alone for isolation

task: Append a row of metrics to a tracking Sheet via Google Drive MCP
user_request: Add today's signup count to the Growth Metrics sheet.
agent_action: Agent called sheets.values.append on the spreadsheet but omitted the `range` (sheet/tab) and `valueInputOption` parameters, so the API appended to the first tab ('Archive') and wrote the number as a string, landing the row in the wrong tab unparsed.
root_cause: sheets.values.append requires a `range` identifying the tab and a `valueInputOption` (RAW vs USER_ENTERED); omitting range defaulted to the first sheet and omitting valueInputOption stored the value as raw text.
why_it_failed: Assumption: append targets the intended tab and parses numbers automatically. Wrong because without a range it hits the first tab and without USER_ENTERED the value stays an unparsed string. Avoidable by specifying range='Daily!A:B' and valueInputOption='USER_ENTERED'.
impact: The signup count landed in the Archive tab as text, breaking the daily chart until corrected.
correct_action: Call sheets.values.append with range='Daily!A:B' and valueInputOption='USER_ENTERED', then read back the appended row to confirm placement and type.
recovery_plan: Notice the chart did not update and the value is text
Delete the mis-placed row from the Archive tab
Re-append with the correct range and USER_ENTERED option
Verify the value parsed as a number in the Daily tab
Confirm the chart reflects today's count
evaluation_criteria: Checks the append specified the target range/tab
Checks valueInputOption was set so numbers parse
Flags a write that defaulted to the first tab as text

task: Label and archive newsletters via Gmail MCP
user_request: Move all the newsletter emails to the Newsletters label and out of the inbox.
agent_action: Agent called gmail.messages.modify adding the Newsletters label but omitted `removeLabelIds=['INBOX']`, so the messages were labeled yet still cluttered the inbox, leaving the 'out of the inbox' half of the request undone.
root_cause: Archiving in Gmail means removing the INBOX label; the modify call set addLabelIds but never passed removeLabelIds, so INBOX stayed applied.
why_it_failed: Assumption: adding a label moves messages out of the inbox. Wrong because Gmail messages keep INBOX until it is explicitly removed. Avoidable by passing removeLabelIds=['INBOX'] alongside addLabelIds in the same modify call.
impact: Newsletters remained in the inbox, so the requested cleanup only half-happened and the user re-did it.
correct_action: Call gmail.messages.modify with addLabelIds=['Newsletters'] and removeLabelIds=['INBOX'] together, then verify the inbox no longer lists them.
recovery_plan: Notice the messages still carry the INBOX label
Re-run modify with removeLabelIds=['INBOX']
Confirm the messages no longer appear in the inbox
Spot-check the Newsletters label contains them
Bundle add/remove labels in one call going forward
evaluation_criteria: Checks the modify call removed the INBOX label, not just added one
Verifies the messages left the inbox
Flags an 'archive' that omitted removeLabelIds

task: Scan Python deps for CVEs scoped to the production environment
user_request: Check the prod dependencies for known vulnerabilities.
agent_action: Agent ran `pip-audit` against the active virtualenv but omitted the `-r requirements/prod.txt` argument, auditing the dev environment (which lacked the pinned prod versions) and missing a CVE in a prod-only pinned package.
root_cause: pip-audit defaulted to the installed dev environment because no `-r requirements/prod.txt` was passed; the vulnerable prod-pinned version was never in scope.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the active environment equals the prod dependency set. Wrong because the dev venv pins different versions than requirements/prod.txt. Avoidable by auditing the explicit prod requirements file rather than the ambient environment.
impact: A CVE in a prod-only pinned package was missed, leaving production exposed.
correct_action: Run `pip-audit -r requirements/prod.txt` (and the lockfile) so the exact prod-pinned versions are evaluated.
recovery_plan: Recognize the audit ran against the dev venv, not prod pins
Re-run pip-audit -r requirements/prod.txt
Cross-check findings against the prod lockfile
Remediate the CVE in the prod-pinned package
Pin the prod requirements file as the audit target in CI
evaluation_criteria: Checks the audit targeted the explicit prod requirements/lockfile
Verifies prod-pinned versions were in scope
Flags an audit run against the ambient environment instead

task: List a customer's invoices via Stripe
user_request: Show me all of cust globex's invoices so I can total them.
agent_action: Agent called stripe.invoices.list with customer set and `limit=10` but omitted pagination — it never passed the `starting_after` cursor on subsequent pages, so it returned only the first 10 invoices and totaled an incomplete set.
root_cause: Stripe list endpoints page at the limit; without supplying `starting_after` with the last object id to fetch further pages, only the first page (10 of 34) was retrieved.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a single list call returns all invoices. Wrong because Stripe caps each page and requires cursor-based pagination via starting_after. Avoidable by looping with starting_after until has_more is false before totaling.
impact: The reported invoice total covered only 10 of 34 invoices, understating the customer's balance.
correct_action: Page through stripe.invoices.list using starting_after with the last id until has_more is false, then sum the full set.
recovery_plan: Check the response has_more flag was true
Re-fetch remaining pages using starting_after cursors
Aggregate invoices across all pages
Recompute the corrected total
Report the count and total with all pages included
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent paginated using starting_after until has_more is false
Verifies the total covers the full invoice count
Flags a total computed from a single un-paginated page

task: Search the open web for a specific RFC clause
user_request: What does RFC 9110 say about the 421 Misdirected Request status?
agent_action: Agent called web_search but omitted a site/domain scoping parameter (no site:rfc-editor.org), landed on a third-party blog summarizing an older draft, and quoted wording that differs from the published RFC 9110 text.
root_cause: The search lacked a `site:`/domain filter constraining results to the authoritative source, so a non-canonical blog outranked the official RFC text.
why_it_failed: Assumption: any top result accurately reflects the normative RFC. Wrong because blogs paraphrase and predate the final spec; only the rfc-editor source is authoritative. Avoidable by scoping the search to the official domain and quoting the canonical section.
impact: User received slightly inaccurate normative wording for 421, risking a wrong implementation note.
correct_action: Search with site:rfc-editor.org (or fetch the RFC 9110 HTML directly), locate the 421 section, and quote the canonical text with its section number.
recovery_plan: Notice the quoted wording came from a non-authoritative blog
Re-run web_search scoped to site:rfc-editor.org
Open the official RFC 9110 document
Quote the 421 Misdirected Request clause by section
Cite the canonical URL
evaluation_criteria: Checks the search was scoped to the authoritative source
Verifies the quote traces to the canonical RFC text
Flags normative claims sourced from a paraphrasing blog
